body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weight compliance as strong evidence but not as final. I am black_litterman and cannot vote for myself. My first choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, Sharpe 0.41, effective N 13.3 and a moderate 4.33% tracking error. Its main weakness is that the 8% volatility floor comes from tuning gamma, and the reviews also note unbiased-noise premises. That is a lesser problem than the fully concentrated or cash-dominated alternatives. Second is cvar_minimization. It is IPS-compliant, has the best backtest Sharpe in the field (0.74) and a contained -18.7% drawdown. It is a tail-aware, covariance-driven method, which fits the late-cycle reasoning in §4.3. The reviewer found no technical error and said the output is the method working as intended. Third is pc_researcher. It has the highest ex-ante Sharpe among the non-extreme candidates (0.51), a 0.70 backtest Sharpe and a 10.9% drawdown. Its two breaches (volatility and tracking error) are on the low side and likely reflect the draft IPS. Reviewers flagged a Sharpe above max_sharpe and a constraint mismatch, so it ranks below the compliant methods. Fourth is max_sharpe. It is compliant with a 0.67 backtest Sharpe, but its 46% single-style concentration and the label mismatch make it fragile to CMA error. Fifth is tail_risk_parity. It adds forecast-free, covariance-based diversification from a different family. Its Sharpe of 0.39 is respectable and its drawdown is small at -7.2%. It breaches return, volatility and tracking error, but the reviews found only a CMA-dependence caveat, not a structural error. Its role is as a defensive sleeve and a family-spanning ensemble member. Why first beats fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier is IPS-compliant and can be built from directly. tail_risk_parity breaches three hard limits and holds mostly cash and short Treasuries, so it can only be a partial sleeve. I flag hierarchical_risk_parity. It holds 91.9% cash, effective N is 1.4 and Sharpe is 0.14. It breaches return, volatility and tracking error, and its own proposal concedes it is not a diversification success. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, because its orthogonality is useful in an ensemble even though it is not in my top five.
